steps.body:
Rotation by angle θ (counterclockwise, about the origin) is the matrix

[[cos θ, −sin θ], [sin θ, cos θ]].

Its columns are where the basis vectors swing to: ⟨1, 0⟩ → ⟨cos θ, sin θ⟩ and ⟨0, 1⟩ → ⟨−sin θ, cos θ⟩ (recall the unit circle). Every point rotates rigidly around the origin.
Don't plug into the formula yet — build the rotation with your hands and see where the formula's entries come from.

widget.prompt: Build the 90° counter-clockwise rotation: send î and ĵ where the turn takes them.
widget.successFeedback: î ↦ (0, 1), ĵ ↦ (−1, 0): that's [[0, −1], [1, 0]] — exactly [[cos 90°, −sin 90°], [sin 90°, cos 90°]]. det = 0·0 − (−1)·1 = 1: rotations never change area.
widget.swappedFeedback: You've put î's landing spot in ĵ's column. Columns are destinations — column 1 is where î goes (straight up to (0, 1)), column 2 is where ĵ goes (left to (−1, 0)).
widget.signFeedback: That's 90° CLOCKWISE — the same turn the other way. Counter-clockwise lifts î UP to (0, 1), so the 1 belongs in the bottom-left, and ĵ swings LEFT to (−1, 0).
widget.fallbackFeedback: Track one basis vector at a time. A quarter-turn counter-clockwise sends î from (1, 0) up to (0, 1) — first column — and ĵ from (0, 1) left to (−1, 0) — second column.

predict.prompt: Which part of a 2×2 matrix tells where the first basis vector lands?
predict.reveal: A matrix's columns are the images of the basis vectors; the transformed grid makes that structural fact visible.

cml.actionGoal: Change matrix entries and observe how columns move basis vectors and transform the plane.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: Change the controlling quantity in this matrixTransform away from the successful state. Which invariant remains true, and which visible consequence changes?

explanation.prompt: Why do matrix columns matter geometrically?

options.label: Each column is where one basis vector lands, and all other vectors follow by linear combination.
options.feedback: Exactly—this identifies the governing mechanism rather than only the final pattern.

options.label: Rows are always the transformed basis arrows.
options.feedback: That describes an appearance or shortcut, not the invariant that makes the relationship hold.

options.label: The determinant alone determines every transformed point.
options.feedback: The live model contradicts that claim when its control is changed.

explanationVariants: A 90° CCW turn sends ⟨3, 2⟩ to ⟨−2, 3⟩ (swap and negate the new x).

options.feedback: That's a CLOCKWISE quarter-turn. CCW gives ⟨−2, 3⟩.
A 90° rotation changes the vector: ⟨−2, 3⟩, not unchanged.

steps.body: Special rotations are clean: **180°** is [[−1, 0], [0, −1]] (negate everything — point reflection through the origin), and **360°** returns the identity [[1, 0], [0, 1]]. Rotation preserves length and angle: it's a **rigid motion** (recall geometry), so magnitudes never change.

explanationVariants: 180° sends every point to its opposite through the origin: ⟨−2, −3⟩.

options.feedback: Right — a half-turn negates both components.
That swaps coordinates (a reflection). A 180° rotation negates both: ⟨−2, −3⟩.
That flips only y. 180° flips BOTH: ⟨−2, −3⟩.

explanationVariants: ⟨3, 2⟩ rotated to ⟨−2, 3⟩ keeps magnitude √13: rotation is a rigid motion, so lengths are unchanged.
Both vectors have length √(9 + 4) = √13 — rotation never resizes.

numericErrors.feedback: √13 ≈ 3.61 — the vector ⟨−2, 3⟩ has the same length as ⟨3, 2⟩, not 5.

explanationVariants: [[0, −1], [1, 0]]·⟨1, 0⟩ = ⟨0, 1⟩ — a 90° CCW turn sends the x-axis unit vector to the y-axis unit vector; its y-component is 1.
⟨1, 0⟩ is the first column's source; after 90° it becomes ⟨0, 1⟩.

approxConstants.label: the original x-component (a 90° CCW turn sends (x, y) → (−y, x), so the new y IS x)

numericErrors.feedback: ⟨1, 0⟩ swings up to ⟨0, 1⟩: the y-component becomes 1.
CCW sends ⟨1, 0⟩ to ⟨0, 1⟩ (y = +1). ⟨0, −1⟩ would be clockwise.

takeaways: Rotation by θ: [[cos θ, −sin θ], [sin θ, cos θ]].
Rotation is rigid: it preserves every length and angle.
steps.teaser: Finale: composing transformations by multiplying matrices.

concept.body: Rotation by θ (CCW): [[cosθ, −sinθ], [sinθ, cosθ]]. 90° → [[0,−1],[1,0]]; 180° → [[−1,0],[0,−1]]. Rotation preserves length.
